test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Average of 17 consecutive natural numbers starting with a is x . What will be the average of 17 consecutive natural numbers starting with a + 6 ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If every term in a set of observations is increased by a constant value **k**, the **average** of the set also increases by **k**.

Original series starts at **a** and new series starts at **a + 6**.

Each term is shifted by **+6** (since **a → a + 6**, **a + 1 → a + 7**, etc.).

New Average = Old Average + Shift = **x + 6**.

**∴ The correct answer is x + 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number of terms (n) = 17, First term = a, Average = x.

**Formula Used:** Average of **consecutive natural numbers** = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3efb6ce68331f6a03e45a1a91e9fa84471252ea824e64f93784072a9ffebbdba.png] 

For the first series starting with **a**:

⇒ Last term = a + (17 − 1) = a + 16

⇒ x = (a + a + 16) ÷ 2

⇒ x = (2a + 16) ÷ 2 = a + 8

For the second series starting with **a + 6**:

⇒ Last term = (a + 6) + (17 − 1) = a + 22

⇒ New Average = ((a + 6) + (a + 22)) ÷ 2

⇒ New Average = (2a + 28) ÷ 2 = a + 14

⇒ New Average = (a + 8) + 6

⇒ New Average = x + 6

**∴ The correct answer is x + 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression (AP)

For any series in AP, the **mean** is always the average of the first and last terms: (a + l) ÷ 2.

Middle Term Property

For an **odd number** of consecutive terms, the average is exactly the middle term of the sequence.

Linear Transformation of Mean

If every value yᵢ = m × xᵢ + c, then the new mean Y = m × X + c, where X is the original mean.
